panels.description: THE THREE PHASES ARE PLOTTED SEPARATELY AND MUST NEVER BE AGGREGATED HERE. A single total series is the cheapest thing to build and would foreclose the phase-triage runbook scenario operations writes in story 8: ADR-0036 §11 decomposes the forward path into three phases precisely because they have DIFFERENT REMEDIES, and an undifferentiated total does not tell an operator which to pursue. The story-8 latency alert gets a scenario of its own and is never folded into egress exhaustion. Per-phase remedies are NOT restated here - see docs/observability/metrics/mh-service.md §Media Forward Path, and the Media Forward Latency by Phase panel on the Media Handler - SLOs dashboard. THE 'total' PHASE IS DELIBERATELY EXCLUDED from this panel by selector. It exists to carry the ADR-0011 objective, because quantiles do not sum and the SLO number needs its own observation; an operator who reads the total first cannot tell which of three remedies to pursue. AND THERE IS NO SERIES MEASURING THE SLI-ELIGIBLE SPAN TODAY. The eligible subset is receive_buffer + processing (MH-internal, not client-influenceable); 'total' is wider and IS client-influenced, because it includes transmit_buffer, which is slow-subscriber time. But the eligible subset is VISIBLE here, not AVAILABLE: p95(receive_buffer + processing) cannot be constructed from p95(receive_buffer) and p95(processing), by the same quantiles-do-not-sum property that justifies 'total' existing at all. So do NOT ratify an objective off these two series - the quantity cannot be computed from what is plotted. A series for the eligible span would only exist if a LATER story narrows the Total phase's recording to end at egress-enqueue; that is an MH hot-path change and this story does not make it. See docs/observability/slos.md §Open: the target. SAMPLED ONE-IN-N: read the sample-ratio panel on the SLOs dashboard before reading any rate off _count. This panel is the phase-triage substrate; the SLOs dashboard carries the objective view.

panels.description: Frames MH discarded on the publisher-to-relay side, broken out by reason - the WHY behind the Media Frame Drops by Direction panel on the Media Handler - Overview dashboard, which answers only WHETHER and on which side. A FLAT LINE AT ZERO MEANS NO DROPS OCCURRED, AND THAT IS THE EXPECTED HEALTHY STATE OF THE LOOPBACK. Every reason in this family is pre-registered at zero at process start (resolve_media_handles), so the healthy reading is a flat zero series, NOT 'No data'. A genuine 'No data' here is a fault in the metrics pipeline - recorder not installed, scrape failing, pod down, or wrong job label - and must never be read as 'no drops occurred'. The sentence this replaces claimed a Prometheus counter materialises no series until first incremented and that 'No data' was therefore the normal reading: true of a lazily-created counter, but never true of THIS family, and it contradicted the present-and-flat-at-zero paragraph below it. There is deliberately no 'or vector(0)' in this query: it would fabricate a series and flatten the by-reason breakdown that triage depends on. TWO REASONS ARE DECLARED BUT CANNOT FIRE TODAY AND ARE NOT LIVE DETECTORS: partial_frame_discard (unreachable until video - audio is one frame per datagram, so the stream-carried path has no producer) and stream_rate_limited (unreachable until uni-streams/video, for the same reason - MH opens no uni-streams this story). A permanently flat series for either is correct, not a fault; do not go looking for a bug behind it. A FLAT PANEL IS AMBIGUOUS AND ALWAYS WILL BE: this family reads present-and-flat-at-zero both when the handler is idle and when no media session ever started, and the two are byte-identical here. Discriminate with Media Session Starts by Outcome first, then with mh_media_frames_dropped_total{reason="transport_receive_dropped"} - flat means no datagram ever arrived, moving means MH received them and never read them. Counted as increase() rather than rate() per ADR-0029 Category A: a single discrete drop under rate() renders as a near-zero rate at any realistic scrape cadence, which reads IDENTICAL TO HEALTHY on the one panel whose purpose is that a single drop is visible. The reason vocabulary and its direction mapping are NOT restated here - see docs/observability/metrics/mh-service.md §Media Forward Path. Zero is healthy: a flat line at zero means no such events occurred. An ABSENT series is NOT a zero — it means the metrics pipeline is broken (recorder not installed, scrape failing, pod down, or wrong job label), not that no events occurred. This panel is not a liveness signal (read the service's traffic/overview panels for liveness), and any non-zero value warrants investigation via the service runbook.
panels.title: Ingress Drops by Reason

panels.title: Egress Drops by Reason

panels.description: Drops on the two reasons whose contract is that they READ ZERO FOREVER: transport_send_refused (the transport seam refused a datagram it should have accepted) and relay_rewrite_failed (rewrite failed on a frame that had already decoded cleanly - an MH bug, never a sender fault). Any non-zero value is an invariant violation, not load shedding. This panel reads 0 rather than 'No data' when no violation has been counted because both reasons are pre-registered at zero at process start (resolve_media_handles), so increase() runs over a present-but-flat series and sums to 0. A noValue:0 override was removed from this panel and must not be reinstated: it never fired (the query returns 0, never an empty result), and now that the series is pre-registered an ABSENT series here would mean the metrics pipeline is broken - recorder not installed, scrape failing, pod down, or wrong job label - which must surface as 'No data' rather than be painted as zero violations. Zero-init is what makes a healthy panel read 0; noValue would only have hidden the faults. Nor are the by-reason breakdown panels empty when healthy - they read present-and-flat-at-zero for exactly the same reason this one does; earlier wording here contrasted this panel against them on that basis and was simply wrong about both. Deliberately NOT the shape of the alert rule that watches this family: this is increase() over the dashboard range, not a rate over a fixed window. Do not copy it into a rule or a rule into it. Zero is healthy: a flat line at zero means no such events occurred. An ABSENT series is NOT a zero — it means the metrics pipeline is broken (recorder not installed, scrape failing, pod down, or wrong job label), not that no events occurred. This panel is not a liveness signal (read the service's traffic/overview panels for liveness), and any non-zero value warrants investigation via the service runbook.
panels.title: Zero-Forever Invariant Drops

panels.description: The fraction of egress attempts the transport accepted, built on the ATTEMPTS SUM (forwarded + dropped) rather than on one addend - a frame count cannot be denominated by anything else, and building on forwarded alone silently rises when drops rise. Expression source: docs/observability/metrics/mh-service.md §Media Forward Path, which is where it is derived and explained; it is reproduced rather than re-derived here. Reads empty in a healthy idle loopback when there are no egress attempts (a legitimate 0/0 ratio). Note the drop panels themselves now read a flat ZERO, not empty (present-at-zero); this ratio can still legitimately read empty on a 0/0. That is not a delivery failure. key_custody=operator: MH cannot read the media it forwards; MC can. A keyless relay working correctly - drops at zero, delivery ratio at 1 - is NOT end-to-end and NOT zero-trust (ADR-0036 §4). Because this is a ratio, an empty panel is a legitimate 0/0 (no egress attempts) and is healthy - do NOT read absence here as a broken pipeline, unlike the by-reason drop panels which are present-at-zero. This panel is not a liveness signal (read the service's traffic/overview panels for liveness), and any non-zero value warrants investigation via the service runbook.
panels.title: Egress Delivery Ratio

panels.description: Egress stream admission decisions (story 2 R-19): one per generation-advancing policy apply, admitted or rejected_stream_ceiling. increase(), NOT rate(): a single discrete rejection under rate() renders as a near-zero rate at any realistic scrape cadence and reads identical to healthy, and a single capacity rejection is exactly what this panel exists to show. Both outcomes are pre-registered at zero at process start, so the healthy reading is a flat zero rejected series, NOT 'No data'. A rejection is a CAPACITY refusal: compare the stream ceiling with the recommended minimum (unsized placeholder budget?) and installed streams with the ceiling (ratchet?) on the panels beside this one. key_custody=operator.
panels.title: Egress Stream Admission Decisions by Outcome

panels.description: Windowed (5-minute sliding) share of admission decisions refused, against the configured threshold - the same bare gauge-to-gauge comparison the egress-exhaustion alert makes, with no PromQL literal. The ratio gauge is authoritative; a rate()-based ratio over the counter uses a different window and WILL differ. 0 decisions in the window reads 0 (idle is silent); all-rejected reads 1. An excursion shorter than a few scrape intervals (the mh-service job's scrape_interval) can be invisible. key_custody=operator.
panels.title: Stream Admission Rejection Ratio vs Threshold

panels.description: Installed egress streams on each handler (mh_media_egress_edges) against its derived egress STREAM ceiling, the ADVISORY recommended minimum, and the edge-limit backstop (mh_media_egress_edges_limit) - all four in one unit, aggregate installed egress streams on the pod. Saturation is edges against the CEILING (capacity; remedy: raise MH_EGRESS_BUDGET_BPS), NEVER against the edge limit: that is a resource guard, and MH refuses to boot with a ceiling above it, so the ceiling always binds first - the limit line is plotted only to show the backstop's headroom. A ceiling below the recommended minimum means the budget is still the unsized placeholder - a configuration state, not an incident; the recommended minimum is never an alert input. Streams are released when a meeting's MC calls EndMeeting (story 2 R-20; MC calls it for every meeting it ends as of story 2 task 12); a meeting whose MC never COMPLETES EndMeeting (an MC crashed or killed before or during teardown; retries exhausted or an MH predating the RPC; a rollback to an MC build without teardown) keeps its streams until the pod restarts (the ratchet), and GC stops placing on a handler at its ceiling - installed streams rising with pod uptime rather than load is that state; recovery is a rollout restart of mh-0/mh-1. Read each pod against ITS OWN ceiling, never against the fleet: MC co-locates each meeting's edges onto ONE handler (chosen by a per-meeting rotation, so pods are roughly balanced across many meetings), but one large meeting's egress is never split and the idle sibling is not headroom for a meeting refused on the busy one. Until capacity-aware spreading lands, a few large meetings can skew the pods; sustained severe skew is worth investigating. key_custody=operator.
panels.title: Installed Egress Streams vs Stream Ceiling

panels.description: The configured egress budget in BYTES per second - the key MH_EGRESS_BUDGET_BPS is in BITS; MH converts once at load, so a factor of 8 between the two is correct. basis=unmeasured records that the budget has no measurement behind it (ADR-0036 open item); this panel deliberately does not select on basis, because that label is designed to change. key_custody=operator.
panels.title: Egress Budget (bytes/s)

panels.description: Meetings each handler holds registered (mh_media_registered_meetings) against MH_MAX_REGISTERED_MEETINGS (mh_media_registered_meetings_limit), story 2 R-21. A RESOURCE GUARD, never capacity and never advertised to GC. Read the gauge as REGISTRATIONS HELD, not meetings in progress: it falls only when an EndMeeting releases a meeting, so a meeting whose MC never COMPLETES EndMeeting (an MC crashed or killed before or during teardown, retries exhausted or an MH predating the RPC, or a rollback to an MC build without teardown) stays counted until the pod restarts. Rising with pod uptime and uncorrelated with load is that residual; many meetings against flat installed streams is the empty-meeting shape the cap exists for. At the limit, NEW meetings are refused (mh_media_policy_applies_total{outcome="rejected_meeting_cap"}) while held ones keep re-asserting. key_custody=operator.
panels.title: Registered Meetings vs Registration Cap

panels.description: EndMeeting decisions (story 2 R-20): released (the registering MC ended the meeting; its registration, routes and edges are reclaimed), unknown_meeting (an acknowledged no-op - MC calls every handler in the assigned set, so this is normal; climbing well above released is an MC-side signal), rejected_ownership (a different mc_id asked to end it; FAILED_PRECONDITION, nothing released - a misrouted or stale MC, or a scope holder acting on a meeting it does not own; see the ownership-reject arm in docs/runbooks/mh-incident-response.md). increase(), NOT rate(): teardowns are low-rate. All three outcomes are pre-registered at zero, so the healthy reading is flat-zero rejects, NOT 'No data'. key_custody=operator.
panels.title: Meeting Teardowns by Outcome

panels.description: Queued forwarding-policy applies MH's session actor REFUSED because the meeting was no longer registered - released by EndMeeting between the apply being queued and the actor reaching it (ADR-0036 section 8; the EndMeetingRequest accepted-residual race). THIS IS THE ONLY SIGNAL THAT THE GUARD WORKS. mh_media_policy_applies_total is recorded only in the gRPC handler, which in this race has already timed out, recorded apply_failed and returned before the queued apply runs, so the actor's refusal is on no other series; and mh_media_registered_meetings staying flat is not evidence either, because flat is also what 'nothing arrived' looks like. Without this panel a guard that silently stopped working looks identical to a guard with nothing to do. NOT rejected_stale: that outcome means a generation strictly lower than the installed one was ignored - a different decision at a different layer - and a flat rejected_stale says nothing about this. NOT disjoint from mh_media_policy_applies_total{outcome="apply_failed"}: one registration can increment both, apply_failed in the handler at deadline expiry and this counter in the actor later. Different denominators; do not sum them and do not build a ratio across them. apply_failed is a NEGATIVE discriminator here, not a positive one: it also covers a full mailbox, an apply timeout, a dead actor and the aggregate egress-edge bound, and it feeds the mh-deployment bake gate. If this panel is flat, an apply_failed near a teardown is one of those other causes. AMBER, NOT RED, and NO ALERT - a non-zero value is the accepted deadline residual occurring and the guard working, so paging on it would page on a design decision deliberately taken. This panel CANNOT show story 4's re-assert fence failing, and its meaning does not change when that fence lands: a re-assert re-registers the meeting, so the guard passes it and this reads flat while the fence fails. Story 4 needs its own signal. Race B (a registration still in flight, ordered MC-side by a wait that rests on client-drop cancellation and fails open) is NOT covered by this counter and has no signal at all; its detection is the registered-meetings ratchet signature, story-2 task 18. Zero is healthy: this counter is zero-init'd at process start, so a healthy reading is a flat 0. An ABSENT series means the metrics pipeline is broken - recorder not installed, scrape failing, pod down, or wrong job label - never 'no late apply arrived'. LAYOUT TRIGGER: this stat sits at w=6 beside Meeting Teardowns, also narrowed to w=6. MeetingTeardownOutcome has three values today and three legend entries survive a quarter-width timeseries. If MH gains a FOURTH teardown outcome, restore Meeting Teardowns to w=12 and move this stat, because four series in a quarter-width legend stops being readable. key_custody=operator.
panels.title: Late Applies Refused (Released Meeting)

panels.description: The ADR-0036 section 8 pre-allocation bounds on ONE registration: MH_MAX_EGRESS_STREAMS_PER_MEETING (mh_media_egress_streams_per_meeting_limit), MH_MAX_CANDIDATE_SOURCES_PER_EGRESS (mh_media_candidate_sources_per_egress_limit) and MH_MAX_MUTED_SOURCES_PER_MEETING (mh_media_muted_sources_per_meeting_limit). A registration exceeding one is refused whole (mh_media_policy_applies_total{outcome="rejected_invalid"}). A CONFIG REFLECTION, not a signal: static for the process lifetime (published once at startup from the one field enforcement reads), so a step here means a pod started on different configuration. No alert selects on it. env-test 01 compares it with the deployed ConfigMap. key_custody=operator.
panels.title: Registration Policy Bounds

panels.description: MH_POLICY_APPLY_TIMEOUT_MS in SECONDS (mh_media_policy_apply_timeout_seconds): the bound on awaiting the session actor's config-apply (and EndMeeting release) reply. A CONFIG REFLECTION, not a signal: static for the process lifetime (published once at startup from the one field enforcement reads), so a step here means a pod started on different configuration. No alert selects on it. env-test 01 compares it with the deployed ConfigMap. key_custody=operator.
panels.title: Policy Apply Timeout

panels.description: The ENFORCED per-stream costs in BYTES per second (MH_STREAM_COST_AUDIO_BPS / MH_STREAM_COST_VIDEO_BPS are bits, converted once at load with div_ceil(8)): mh_media_stream_cost_audio_bytes_per_second and mh_media_stream_cost_video_bytes_per_second. The heavier one divides the budget into mh_media_egress_stream_ceiling. Deliberately NOT on the Egress Budget panel. A CONFIG REFLECTION, not a signal: static for the process lifetime (published once at startup from the one field enforcement reads), so a step here means a pod started on different configuration. No alert selects on it. env-test 01 compares it with the deployed ConfigMap. key_custody=operator.
panels.title: Per-Stream Egress Costs (bytes/s)

title: Media Handler - Media Path
description: MH media-path triage board: where an operator answers WHY, after mh-overview has answered WHETHER. key_custody=operator - media is encrypted between clients; MH, transport and storage cannot read it; MC can. That is accepted operator custody, NOT end-to-end and NOT zero-trust.
